title: How To: Configure BGP on Switch Engine (EXOS)

remediation_steps.description: Create, Configure, and Enable Loopback (optional) interfaces Create VLAN interfaces to communicate with other systems: create vlan <vlan-name>
Assign an IP address on each VLAN interface: configure vlan <vlan-name> ipaddress <ip>/<mask>
Add ports on each VLAN: configure vlan <vlan-name> add ports <ports> untagged
Create a loopback interface and assign an IP address (used as BGP router ID): create vlan <loopback_x> configure vlan <loopback_x> ipaddress <ip>/<mask>
Enable loopback mode on the loopback interface: enable loopback-mode vlan <loopback_x>

Verify the vlan information (Example Output from R11): BGP-R11.1 # show vlan Untagged ports auto-move: Inform -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Name            VID  Protocol Addr       Flags
Add routes for the BGP neighbor's loopback interface : configure iproute add <NBR_LOOPBACK_IP>/<MASK> <NEXTHOP>
Enable IP forwarding on the VLAN(s) and loopback interface: enable ipforwarding <vlan>
Configure BGP Router ID: configure bgp routerid <id>
Configure the local AS number for the switch: configure bgp AS-number <ASN>

configuration_example.scenario: This article demonstrates how to configure the Boarder Gateway Protocol (BGP) on Extreme Switching devices running Switch Engine (EXOS).

additional_notes: Switch Engine (Universal & Summit) Base License Support:BGP Auto-peering - all universal platforms but limited to X465, X590, X690, and X695 Summit platformsBGP peers--Switches are allowed up to 2 manually configured BGP peers on the default VR; however, no support for Summit platformsSwitch Engine Premier (Universal) and Core (Summit) License Support:BGP4 and MBGP (BGP4+) for IPv4 ECMP requires a Premier license and is supported on all universal platformsBGP4 and MBGP (BGP4+) for IPv4 ECMP requires a Core license on Summit platforms (X450G2, X460G2, X465, X590, X690, and X695)BGP4 and MBGP (BGP4+) for IPv6 requires a Premier license for Switch Engine and is supported on all universal platformsBGP4 and MBGP (BGP4+) for IPv6 requires a Core license on Summit platforms (X450G2, X460G2, X465, X590, X690, and X695)For additional information, please check the Feature license requirements guides:SwitchEngine_Feature_License_Requirements_32.7.1.pdfEXOS_Feature_License_Requirements_32.7.1.pdf
